\begin{table}[!t]
\centering
\footnotesize
\caption{Judging density on the hybrid first stage, averaged over re-rankers and windows. ``Judged@10'' is the mean fraction of the returned top ten that carries a relevance judgment; ``condensed $\Delta$'' recomputes the paired difference after removing unjudged documents from both rankings. The condensed $\Delta$ is a diagnostic, not a like-for-like robustness check: with a judged fraction of the top ten near 0.10, the condensed top ten holds about one judged document, so condensation changes the depth scored as well as the list. The standard-nDCG gains do not survive as magnitudes under it (median condensed-to-standard ratio 0.0000 over the 213 significant cells), and the corpus-level non-negativity shown here is an averaging effect: 18 of those 213 cells have a negative condensed $\Delta$ and 154 are exactly zero. What the judged densities do support is that the re-ranker does not inflate unjudged documents. See Section~VI-C.}
